history.period: Ancient origins (Puranic references); present structure 1734 CE
history.summary: One of the 12 Jyotirlingas; the swayambhu lingam faces south (Dakshinamukhi), the only Jyotirlinga to do so, symbolising mastery over death. Scriptural mentions appear in the Skanda Purana, the Mahabharata and Kalidasa's Meghaduta. The original temple is attributed to the Paramara rulers of Malwa (sources variously cite the 8th and 11th centuries - verify); it was destroyed in 1234-35 CE when Iltutmish raided Ujjain, and the lingam was thrown into the nearby Kotiteerth Kunda. The present structure was rebuilt in 1734 CE by the Maratha general Ranoji Shinde (under Peshwa Bajirao I), funded in large part by his diwan Ramchandra Baba Shenavi, with later additions by Mahadji Shinde, Baiza Bai and Jayajirao Shinde; Ahilyabai Holkar's patronage is also credited by some sources (conflict - verify). The temple is famous for the daily Bhasma Aarti and is central to the Simhastha Kumbh Mela. Today it is managed under the Ujjain district collectorate. No CSV town/state errors.

name: Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga
town_description: Ancient city on the Shipra (Kshipra) River in Madhya Pradesh, one of Hinduism's seven Sapta Puri, home to the Mahakaleshwar Jyotirlinga and the Simhastha Kumbh Mela held every 12 years.

travel.airport: Devi Ahilya Bai Holkar Airport, Indore (~55 km)
travel.railway: Ujjain Junction, connected to all major stations of India
travel.road: Well connected by road; regular buses from Indore, Bhopal and other MP cities

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Maha Shivaratri and Shravan draw very large crowds
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported 3:00 AM-11:00 PM; timings vary on festivals (verify)
